entries.title: Experience the art and legacy of Dr. Esther Mahlangu
entries.summary: A portrait of Dr Nontobeko Ntombela, Senior Lecturer, Department of Curatorial, Public and Visual Cultures, Wits School of Arts, University of the Witwatersrand
entries.content:
Today we’re sharing the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture, honoring her pioneering spirit on her 91st birthday. More than 45 stories and a rich archive covering her art, life, and legacy are now accessible to a global audience.

For many years, I have worked closely with Esther and her family. It’s a relationship built on years of research and a deep admiration for her as both an artist and a person. It was out of this long-standing connection that the vision for “‘Then I Knew I Was Good at Painting’: Esther Mahlangu, a Retrospective,” was born.

My goal has always been to present a comprehensive exploration of her life and work, contributing to my long-standing research on South African women artists who have made an impact on the arts since the early 20th century.

Through my research, I gathered a rich collection of her work, including large-scale murals, intimate pieces, and rare archival materials. But the archives didn’t include anything from her life before 1980, so crucial pieces of her history were missing. This void challenged us to find new ways to tell her full story.

A collaboration session with Esther Mahlangu, Nontobeko Ntombela, and the Google team.

In collaboration with Google Arts & Culture, we used AI to visually recreate Esther’s undocumented memories. The process brought us closer to her work and prompted further recollections from Esther herself.

This project brought our curatorial and archival work together with the technical expertise of Google DeepMind and Google Arts & Culture Lab, alongside research and design studio Domestic Data Streamers’ synthetic memories initiative. Through a series of workshops and interviews, we were able to document a missing period of Mam' Esther's history, from when she started painting at age 10 until her first documented works in 1980. These stories — such as the moment she discovered her talent for painting as a 10-year-old using feathers instead of a brush — became the source material for our work. Following the methodology from the synthetic memories initiative and using archival material, the team generated still images based on Esther’s memories. They then used Veo to turn the images into videos that brought Esther's early days to life.

The stories also contribute to the online archive of Esther’s life on Google Arts & Culture. More than 45 exhibitions, curated in collaboration with Art of Contemporary Africa, Iziko Museums of South Africa, the British Museum, the Jean Pigozzi Collection, the National Museum of Women in the Arts, and Serpentine, tell the story of how she came to be known in the world, through her artwork, archives, Street View, and more.

This project demonstrates a new way to approach the preservation of cultural heritage, with technology that’s guided at every step by a respect for personal memory and historical accuracy.

It is my hope that this retrospective cements Esther’s place as a pivotal voice in global contemporary art, invites audiences to reimagine the possibilities of her archive, and ensures her story and her artistic vision can inspire generations to come.

Explore the exhibition at goo.gle/esther-mahlangu.

entries.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
entries.summary: A man speaks into a phone. Text on the screen reads 'Gemini Intelligence'
entries.content:
Gemini Intelligence 1 brings the best of Gemini to Android devices, helping your devices work harder for you. Earlier this year, we announced Gemini Intelligence, and this summer devices started rolling out — from the Pixel 11 to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Flip8 and S26 series. 2 Today, we’re introducing new features built for Gemini Intelligence, and expanding capabilities to more of Android’s most advanced devices. 3 Here’s a look at what’s new.

Gemini Intelligence on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10

Gemini Intelligence is coming to even more devices. Motorola is introducing its first Gemini Intelligence device, motorola signature 27, which is available for pre-order in the U.S. on November 19. And with today’s Pixel Drop, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold get the latest features for Gemini Intelligence.

Alongside this expansion, we’re bringing some of our favorite capabilities to more devices and regions, helping handle the busywork so you can focus on what matters. Rambler 4 — which turns spoken thoughts into clean, organized text in real-time — is now available on Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10, Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold, as well as the new motorola signature 27. And task automation 5 — which lets you ask Gemini to handle logistics like ordering food, hailing rides, or booking reservations across your favorite apps — is expanding to the UK, India, and Japan.

Build custom widgets with a prompt

Create My Widget 6 , which is rolling out over the next few weeks, lets you design a personalized widget with a simple description in your own words — no coding required. Whether you want a dashboard for your upcoming trip, a monthly spending tracker, or a race day countdown, Create My Widget can pull in information from Gmail, Calendar, and Search to create a custom widget just for you, giving you the information you want at a glance on your homescreen.

Get personalized tech support with Device Assistance

Device Assistance 7 helps you control, change, or fix your device by just asking your phone for help. Ask Gemini to clear up space on your device, check which apps can access your location, or mute distractions while making sure important calls still come through. Gemini deeply understands your device so it can act as your personal device expert.

Experience proactive help across a range of screens

Gemini Intelligence is designed to support you across whatever screen you’re using. Last month we launched Googlebook, the first laptop designed for Gemini Intelligence.

And if you have a Pixel phone with Gemini Intelligence, it will soon bring proactive suggestions to Android Auto — connecting the dots across your apps to surface helpful, personalized suggestions 8 when you need them. For example, if your friend texts you to ask where you are meeting for a pilates class, Gemini Intelligence on Android Auto can find your confirmation email and instantly suggest sending the address with a single tap.

Plus, in the next few weeks, Create My Widget is coming to Pixel Watch. You’ll be able to design widgets that keep the details that matter to you right on your wrist.

entries.title: Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence, custom widgets, and more in our November Pixel Drop
entries.summary: Pixel Drop text with the Google G logo and irridescent squares
entries.content:
Our November Pixel Drop is here, with new and expanded features making your Pixel devices more personalized, intuitive, and handy. See how we’re bringing smarter automation, next-level personalization, and upgraded connectivity to your favorite devices. Updates start rolling out today and will continue over the next several weeks.

Use Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence

Gemini Intelligence is now available on Pixel 10 devices, bringing new capabilities like Rambler, personalized suggestions, and taking care of multi-step tasks — like placing your morning coffee order.

Polish your messages with Rambler on Pixel 10: Voice typing just got a major upgrade. Rambler can automatically remove filler words like “um,” and format your thoughts into clear, polished text. Just speak naturally, review, and send.

Complete multi-step tasks with Gemini: Whether you’re getting groceries, booking a ride, ordering takeout, or trying to find a reservation at your favorite restaurant, let Gemini handle the logistics so you can focus on other tasks. Now available in Japan, UK, and India.

Receive proactive suggestions: From sharing your ETA with a tap when someone asks when you’ll arrive, to helping you find the perfect dinner spot, your Pixel anticipates what you need with timely information and suggested actions, so you can accomplish your daily tasks faster. 1 Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4.

Create more personalized widgets: Ever find yourself wanting a widget that doesn’t seem to exist? Create personalized widgets, like a tracker to follow your monthly spending, a game day widget with your team colors, or a getaway countdown that automatically pulls in flight and reservation details. Your home screen can be as personalized as you want it to be. Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5. 2

Catch up on long conversations: Your Pixel can now provide summaries of your longer conversations, so you can see what’s important right away. Now available in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Hindi, and Traditional Chinese. Coming to Pixel Watches soon. 3

Call Screen got an upgrade on Pixel 11 series

Whenever you see a call from an unknown number and choose to screen it, Gemini will ask unknown callers why they're reaching out in a much more conversational manner handling the exchange until you decide to jump in or end the call. With a live transcript displayed right on your screen, you can easily follow along and decide exactly when to pick up. Also, coming to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 soon. 4

Personalize your Pixel with new custom icon styles

Following the launch of Custom Icons earlier this year, we’re adding more styles to give you even more ways to personalize your home screen Pixel. Pick from distinct styles that apply across all your app icons on the home screen. 5

New updates coming to Pixel search

Now available on Pixel 6 and newer devices, Pixel search helps you find what you need across your phone – from vacation photos and recent emails to messages, calendar events, and device settings. 6

Stay in the moment with Google Messages and HiLight

HiLight now supports Google Messages. When your phone is face down, HiLight will glow if you receive a message from one of your favorite contacts — letting you stay present without missing important messages or calls. 7

Keep tabs on your belongings with Pixel Tag

Pixel Tag offers peace of mind so you always know where your most important things are — and it’s available November 11. It’s slim enough to fit in your wallet and durable enough to attach to your belongings, with a battery that lasts over a year. The Find Hub network of more than 1 billion Android devices helps you locate your belongings even if they are miles away and UWB enables visual direction and distance guidance to find it nearby. 8 Pixel Tag is available starting November 11 for $29.99 for one or $99.99 for a four-pack.

Switch between two of America's best 5G networks with Google Fi

Starting today on eligible Pixels, Google Fi’s new super network delivers the nation's fastest, most expansive coverage by automatically switching between two of America's top 5G cellular networks and millions of secure Wi-Fi networks. 9 10 11 12 Already have a Pixel but not using Google Fi? Get 50% off on select unlimited plans for 12 months. Ends 12/1/26. All terms apply. Visit the blog post, Google Fi website for details, and join Google Fi today.

Unlock your Pixel Watch with your phone

Your Pixel devices work better together. When your watch is on your wrist and you’ve unlocked your nearby phone, your Pixel Watch will automatically unlock so you can skip typing your PIN or pattern on the watch. Coming in the next few weeks. 13

Step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch

We’re now rolling out step-by-step workouts to Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. Whether you’re following an exercise routine created by your Google Health Coach 14 or a custom workout built in the Google Health app, you can get step-by-step instructions, log reps and weights, and track metrics directly from your Pixel Watch or your phone.

Check out our community forum post for the full list of new features arriving on your Pixel devices this month.

entries.title: Get step-by-step workout guidance on your Pixel Watch.
entries.summary: Get live workout guidance on your Pixel Watch with Google. Follow custom routines and track reps directly on your wrist. See how it works.
entries.content:
Step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch 3 and newer models, starting today. This feature, first announced with the launch of Pixel Watch 5, provides live guidance on your watch during each exercise in your workout.

Whether you’re following a personalized workout from the Google Health Coach 1 or a custom exercise routine manually built in the Google Health app, you can view step-by-step instructions on your Pixel Watch or on your phone. The experience stays synchronized between both devices, and after you end your workout, you will see your stats in the app and on your watch.

You can also log reps and weights on your wrist, and view your live metrics on your watch or phone to stay motivated on the path to your health goals.

entries.title: Introducing Google Fi’s new super network
entries.summary: A cityscape at sunset overlaid with light trails, featuring the text "Don't bet on a single signal." and the Google Fi Wireless logo.
entries.content:
Google Fi Wireless is launching our new super network, automatically switching you between two of America’s best 5G cellular networks and millions of premium Wi-Fi networks. Powering all our plans on eligible Google Pixel phones, it brings you the fastest speeds and most expansive coverage in the nation. 1 It’s our greatest innovation in connectivity yet.

Automatic switching between two 5G networks

Rolling out starting today on Pixel 9 and newer phones, every Google Fi plan includes access to two of America’s fastest 5G networks. 2 3 Unlike other major carriers, only Google Fi automatically switches you between the networks in real time. 4 5 If your primary connection drops, Google Fi moves you to a secondary data connection so you can stay on a strong, reliable signal—hitting fewer dead zones on the highway, down country roads, and wherever else your day takes you.

Faster speeds in crowds with millions of Wi-Fi networks

Even with great cellular coverage, indoor spaces like airports and malls can get crowded. Now available in millions of more locations around the country, Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ seamlessly connects you to high-quality Wi-Fi in millions of locations without the hassle of going into your settings or logging in. 6 Plus, unlike other major carriers, we secure your connection with automatic encryption, keeping your online activity private. 5 7

Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ is available on Pixel devices and is rolling out to select Samsung and Motorola phones, so even more devices can get faster speeds in crowded places. 6

A global super network at no extra cost

Our super network keeps up with your travels around the globe. Network switching and Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ are available internationally, so your travel apps and messaging are ready to go the moment you arrive abroad. 3 8 It’s included in our Unlimited Premium and Flexible plans at no extra cost.

Personalized service

Get instant account help and troubleshooting from Ask Fi, our new support agent powered by Google AI, directly in the Fi app. Whether you need connectivity troubleshooting or have a quick question about billing, you can get reliable, helpful answers when you need them.

Limited-time promotions

For new subscribers, get $500 off instantly and $599 back over 24 monthly credits when you purchase the new Google Pixel 11 Pro, plus $10/mo service credit for 2 years with the Unlimited Premium plan. Ends 11/18/26. Terms apply.

Already have a Pixel but not using Google Fi? Get 50% off select unlimited plans for 12 months. Ends 12/1/26. Terms apply. Visit the Google Fi website for details, and join Google Fi today.

entries.content:
Starting today, developers can build with Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. Built for sustained agentic workflows, Carbon tackles complex, multi-step problems across software engineering, full-stack web development, scientific research, and shows strong cybersecurity capabilities. With stronger alignment and reliable follow-through, it helps you stay focused on building and shipping great, secure products.

Start building using the paid tier of the API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, and Google AI Ultra subscribers can try it in AI Studio and our agent-first development platform, Google Antigravity.

  • Check out the Gemini API Developer Guide for model details and setup instructions.
  • Read the Google Antigravity blog for details on using Carbon in our agent-first development platform.

entries.title: Introducing the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark
entries.summary: Text "Visual Knowledge Work" next to the Gemini 4 logo and an illustration of documents
entries.content:
In partnership with Artificial Analysis, we're launching MKA (Multimodal Knowledge Agent), a new benchmark built to evaluate how agents reason across visually complex files to solve real-world knowledge work tasks.

Introducing MKA

Most knowledge work benchmarks can be solved with text alone, without ever needing to look at an image or page layout. Yet, everyday professional work looks very different. Across many industries, day-to-day work is deeply visual — from cross-referencing architectural blueprints and tracing engineering schematics to synthesizing findings into polished decks, reports, and spreadsheets. We built MKA to measure how well agents can handle this visually complex work.

To ground the benchmark in real-world workflows, we partnered with domain experts across 10 verticals and 83 occupations where day-to-day work is inherently visual. Together, these specialists — from architects and biologists to underwriters and data scientists — created MKA's 200-task evaluation set to assist them in their jobs.

MKA's 10 verticals.

Each task reflects a multi-step project that takes a seasoned professional three to eight hours to complete, pairing a realistic prompt and a bundle of multimodal input files with an expert-written rubric of roughly 70 yes/no checks, weighted 75% on factual accuracy and 25% on visual design.

Three MKA tasks, from prompt and input files to golden output and rubric.

Starting today, you can explore the benchmark and evaluate your own models on Artificial Analysis. Every model runs in the same open-source agent harness, Stirrup, with the same tools, sandbox, and turn budget.

An agentic autorater built on a non-Google model grades each deliverable. It opens every file, renders pages, inspects spreadsheet formulas, and checks the work against the expert rubric. When domain experts graded model outputs themselves, they agreed with the autorater 96% of the time.

To keep results meaningful, Artificial Analysis runs the 200-task evaluation set and keeps it private so the tasks can't leak into training data or be found by the model via search. We've also released a separate set of 10 public tasks on Hugging Face, so anyone can inspect the format and test their own agents.

Our technical report covers the methodology and results in detail. It shows that frontier models work in very different ways. On the same tasks, the models we tested have extreme differences in efficiency, using between 30 and 130 turns on average to complete each task. We show how strong perception abilities are necessary to solve each task, and we also show how models try and fail to compensate when vision is removed.

Expanding visual frontiers with Gemini 4 Carbon

Gemini 4 Carbon achieves #2 in quality among the models we tested, and completes tasks at 6x lower cost on average compared to the top scoring model.

Gemini 4 Carbon is on the pareto frontier of quality and price for the MKA eval.

Getting started

Gemini 4 Carbon is available today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio. Explore our updated Gemini 4 developer guide and documentation to get started.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
entries.summary: an illustrated carbon with several number 4's around it
entries.content:
Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning.

Two weeks ago, we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program. Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops.

Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity’s WANDR, and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model.

To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing 

/swarm
in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change.

Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, at the same introductory price 1 as Gemini 4 Argon ($2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens). It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search.

Higher-precision knowledge work, artifact generation, and data analysis

Across legal, finance, and enterprise operations, Gemini 4 Carbon combines frontier visual understanding, reasoning, and exhaustive retrieval to synthesize grounded insights across large sets of dense documents and data. It follows strict schemas and formatting to generate polished and precise spreadsheets, presentations, and reports.

Existing benchmarks don’t adequately capture how agents reason natively over dense files with charts, images, blueprints, schematics, and tables, so we partnered with Artificial Analysis to launch the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark that tests a model’s multimodal performance in agentic workflows. Carbon ranks #2 while being more than 6X lower in average cost per task compared to the top performing model.

In pre-release evaluations, Carbon matched the performance of the best model tested on deep financial research on Hebbia’s E2E Financial Agentic evaluation, and ranked at the top out of 23 frontier model configurations on Balyasny Asset Management’s General Financial Intelligence benchmark, spanning legal expertise, agentic tool use and execution, coding and data engineering, and perception and context understanding.

Improved agentic coding, full stack development, and 3D and UI design

Carbon performs exceptionally well on engineering tasks that require multi-agent collaboration like multi-package migrations, cross-subsystem root-cause investigations, and complex architectural redesigns. For web app development, it runs build-and-verify loops, recovers from errors, and checks both its code and the rendered UI to produce complete, working applications. Stronger visual design, spatial reasoning, and attention to environmental detail also carry over to 3D game development and creative coding.

Frontier cybersecurity capabilities

Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber delivers our strongest cybersecurity capabilities to date, giving security teams the end-to-end intelligence they need in protecting critical software. When accessed through the Fairwind Program, Carbon leads on key benchmarks across finding (SEC-bench Pro), exploiting (ExploitGym), and patching (CWE-bench v1) vulnerabilities: inspecting software, tracing how flaws can be chained together across systems, and generating verified root-cause patches.

Early testers inside and outside of Google are already seeing strong results with Carbon for cyber in practice.

  • In Project Fortify, Google’s autonomous system spanning scanning, triage, and remediation, Carbon hit 100% recall on scanning and 95% precision on triage, on our internal benchmark. On Open Source code repository testing we see an over 25% relative improvement on Argon's already strong recall rate, surfacing previously undetected, real-world logic flaws. Bringing these gains across Google, one of the world’s largest users of open-source software, helps secure both our own systems and the broader ecosystem.
  • Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research (CVR) team recently used Carbon to prove that two bugs in a popular open-source software were in fact exploitable vulnerabilities, comparable in severity to the recent PHP2Shell exploit. By using Carbon to build a proof of concept, CVR helped maintainers re-classify the bug as critical and swiftly issue a patch. Details will be shared after the responsible disclosure process completes.
  • As part of Wiz’s Scan for Good program, the team used Carbon to assess vulnerabilities in public digital infrastructure. For example, when scanning two major SaaS providers, the model uncovered 0-day vulnerabilities in under two hours compressing weeks of vulnerability research to a single afternoon. The team partnered with the impacted organizations to remediate in record time, helping to mitigate potential impact on tens of thousands of companies.

Stronger scientific and mathematical reasoning

Gemini 4 Carbon shows strongly improved performance in reasoning across physics, math, and life sciences, synthesizing experimental data, testing hypotheses, and reasoning through multi-step domain problems. For drug toxicity research company Axiom Bio, Carbon is now the leading model in performance for translational science, finding novel mechanisms of toxicity they hadn’t found previously. Axiom is now moving their production scientific analyses and agents to both Carbon and Argon to unlock the creation of safer drugs.

Researchers across Google have been using Carbon in Google Antigravity to accelerate their work:

  • Code verification: Researchers built a new agentic framework for formal verification called AlphaProof Code and put it to work on a major security challenge: mathematically proving the actual code underlying the cryptographic protocol of Signal. Using Carbon alongside other models, our researchers translated security goals to mathematical theorems. AlphaProof Code agents then used Carbon to generate millions of lines of code in Lean, a computer language for writing mathematical proofs, helping them prove key security properties in weeks — a task that historically takes expert teams years. The result indicates Carbon’s potential to unlock scalable formal verification, long considered a gold-standard approach to building secure software.
  • Enzyme assay development: Provided with only lab notebooks and raw data, Carbon went beyond standard analysis to surface hard-to-interpret data anomalies, which it used to diagnose subtle wet lab experimental artifacts such as incomplete automated mixing in deep wells, leading to substantially improved reproducibility. Moreover Carbon improved methods to deconvolute chromatography peaks and caught trace sample carryover in research instruments, significantly accelerating the development of new assays and tightening the feedback loop between computation and the bench.
  • Protein structure prediction: Structure prediction models like AlphaFold 3 use Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) of evolutionary relatives to help infer how amino acid chains fold. As a result they often struggle on understudied, viral, microbial, and eukaryotic proteins that have very few matches in standard databases. Working in a multi-agent setup, our researchers used Gemini 4 Carbon to autonomously discover remote homologs across petabase-scale unannotated sequence archives, environmental and viral sequence catalogs, and 3D structure databases. For example, across 7 low-homolog protein families from the CASP17 blind test set, Carbon increased the number of homologs retrieved by 40-fold on average, greatly increasing the information available to structure prediction models without need for retraining. While broader benchmarking is still underway, addressing this upstream search bottleneck potentially offers a promising path toward modeling hard-to-characterize regions of the proteome.

Four weeks ago, we opened applications to give 10,000 scientists access to Argon in Google Antigravity free of charge for six months to accelerate the pace of their research, and we’ve onboarded thousands of scientists already. Today, we’re expanding access to Carbon for current and future participants, and going forward, the program will continue providing access to our latest frontier models as they become available. Applications remain open and onboarding continues on a weekly rolling basis, subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection.

Progress in model safety and security

With each new model release, we continue to strengthen our safety and security mitigations, agentic misuse prevention, model alignment, and harm reduction proportionately with model capability.

Because Gemini 4 Carbon introduces stronger cyber capabilities we build on Argon’s strong safety and security stack to fortify robustness to misuse and prompt injection.

  • Mitigating frontier safety misuse risks: We’ve strengthened our misuse safeguards to help ensure stronger defensive reasoning does not translate into offensive risk. In simulated cyberattack testing environments seeded with ExploitBench and CyScenarioBench, Carbon blocked 99% of attack trajectories from our adaptive red-teaming agent that can iteratively revisit its attack plans after each block. The Carbon safeguards lowered the per-attempt breach rate to just 0.8% (down from 3.1% on Argon). Our safeguards also lowered the automated cyberattack query success rate to 2.17% in Gray Swan’s testing, compared to 9.86% on Argon. And external testing by Trajectory Labs found zero new universal jailbreaks across 132 hours and over 13,000 requests.
  • Promoting safe and aligned model interactions: When we announced Carbon, we showed significant improvements in alignment as measured by our monitor flag rates across the model’s lifecycle, as well as reductions in data fabrication. New results show that on our 375-task agentic honesty benchmark, it passed 92% of tasks (compared to 70% for Argon) — declining to fill in missing experimental data 98% of the time and flagging methodological flaws 68% of the time.
  • Protecting users from indirect prompt injection attacks: Two weeks ago, we shared that Carbon achieved a 0% prompt injection attack success rate on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark — marking the first time that milestone has been reached. At the same time, we know that prompt injection robustness remains an area for continued improvement. Our advanced automated red teaming continues to push the limits here and has shown that models could be further improved against sophisticated attacks in some distributions. It provides the data for us to continuously advance our models’ security to the next frontier.

For more details, read the full Gemini 4 Carbon Safety and Security report.

Getting started with Gemini 4 Carbon

Starting today, Carbon joins Argon in our family of frontier models across our products:

  • For developers: Build with the Gemini API paid tier in AI Studio and Android Studio, and if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber, you can try it in Google Antigravity and AI Studio.
  • For enterprises: Try it in Gemini for business via the API or model drop down, Google Antigravity, or CodeMender.
  • For everyday users: Try Carbon starting today in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber.
  • For scientists & researchers: Apply for a chance to get access to both Argon and Carbon via Google Antigravity’s highest usage tier free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection.
  • For cybersecurity defenders: Apply to join the Fairwind Program to get access to Carbon for cyber on a rolling basis.

See the model card to learn more about Gemini 4 Carbon and to start building with it, explore our updated Gemini 4 developer guide and documentation for best practices on migrating workflows to the model.

entries.title: Introducing 3 new domains: .eat, .fly, and .here
entries.summary: Illustration of a traveler with a laptop and suitcase under a flying airplane, a woman eating a chicken wing next to a plate of wings and chips, and a woman in a red apron tapping a location pin on a map.
entries.content:
Three new top-level domains launch today: .eat, .fly, and .here. Each one gives businesses and individuals a clear, memorable address that tells people what they can do before they even click.

Grab a bite to .eat

From running a restaurant to finding a table, the businesses behind every meal are on .eat. Here’s what’s cooking:

  • Wingstop is known for its made-to-order chicken wings in bold flavors. Explore how Wingstop serves the world flavor at wingstop.eat.
  • Clayton Farms owns and operates quick serve restaurants that grow their greens on site. They are mapping where America can and cannot get fresh food at america.eat.
  • Ghips makes premium potato chips cooked in grass-fed ghee. Snack differently at ghips.eat.
  • Xook is a robotic kiosk that makes fresh salads and bowls. Order at xook.eat.
  • Kinro helps restaurant owners explore insurance options with licensed agents. Compare coverage at insurance.eat.

Take off on .fly

From aircraft that inspect the power grid to AI that books your next trip, .fly is home to businesses on the move. Here are a few already taking off:

  • Caddy is a personal AI that lives in iMessage and WhatsApp. One text and it plans the trip, books flights and hotels, and handles changes at caddy.fly.
  • Canary verifies AI-generated code during development, helping teams find and fix bugs before they ship. See how at canary.fly.
  • Voltair builds long-range drones that inspect power lines. See them at voltair.fly.
  • Onfly is building an AI travel assistant for business trips. Book, change, or cancel by chat, all on.fly.
  • Flycode helps subscription businesses recover failed payments, so fewer customers slip away over a declined card. Learn more at flycode.fly.

Be right .here

From your next apartment to your next job to your next blood test, .here is where people get things done. A few places to start:

  • Zillow helps people find their next home. Search for an apartment to rent.here or sell your home at sell.here.
  • Rocket Lawyer provides AI and attorney support for everything legal. Find a lawyer.here.
  • Apply gives candidates a verified profile and matches them with jobs from employers that fit them. Find your next role at apply.here.
  • Pocket Worlds builds social virtual worlds where millions meet, create, and play. Step inside at worlds.here.
  • SiPhox Health brings blood testing home. Collect a sample, mail it to a certified lab, and track your results at bloodtest.here.

Hungry, headed somewhere, or ready to get to work? Find your .eat, .fly, or .here domain through your registrar of choice. Starting today, you can register available domains through our Early Access Program for an additional one-time fee that decreases daily until November 17, 2026. At 16:00 UTC on November 17, all three will be publicly available at a base annual price, without the one-time extra fee.

entries.title: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps.
entries.summary: Google and Adobe are integrating creative and productivity tools. Edit PDFs in Drive and use Adobe AI in Gemini. See what’s new in this partnership.
entries.content:
Today at Adobe MAX, we announced we’re expanding our partnership with Adobe.

Switching between apps to edit a PDF or fine-tune an image can quickly break your focus. Our partnership will bring Adobe’s creative and productivity tools directly into the Google products you use every day. It will also bring Google’s frontier AI models into Adobe’s apps. Here’s what’s coming:

  • Work faster with PDFs: You’ll soon have a direct pathway from Google Drive and Gmail into Adobe Acrobat, surfaced as a suggested app across both services, including an “Edit with” entry point in file previews.
  • Create right where you search and chat: Adobe is expanding its connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise with Acrobat and additional creative tools. Adobe will also bring its creative tools to AI Mode in Google Search.
  • Powering creatives and enterprises: Businesses will be able to use Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker agent in Gemini Enterprise — an AI assistant that helps teams design graphics, work with PDFs, and launch marketing campaigns without switching apps.
  • Exploring editing experiences with DeepMind: Adobe and Google DeepMind will explore new editing capabilities for creative professionals, starting with an image model for Photoshop that could enable near-real-time edits.
